title: Compass calibration error
shortDescription: The drone's compass is detecting magnetic interference or is miscalibrated.
fullDescription:
DJI drones use a magnetometer (compass) to determine orientation relative to magnetic north. When the compass reads inconsistent values, flight is blocked or restricted to ATTI mode.

Causes include nearby metal structures, rebar in concrete, power lines, or relocating the drone to a significantly different geographic area without recalibrating. The app prompts a calibration dance that should be done outdoors away from metal.

Flying with an uncalibrated compass risks flyaways and erratic behavior, so DJI disables GPS-dependent flight modes until the issue is resolved.

causes.cause: Nearby magnetic interference (metal, power lines, cars)
Drone moved to new geographic region

symptoms: Compass error warning in DJI Fly/Go app

fixSteps.title: Move to open area
fixSteps.instruction: Go to an open outdoor field away from buildings, power lines, and vehicles.

fixSteps.title: Start compass calibration
fixSteps.instruction: In DJI Fly/Go app, go to aircraft settings and select Compass Calibration.

fixSteps.title: Perform calibration dance
fixSteps.instruction: Rotate drone 360 degrees horizontally, then 360 degrees vertically (nose down) as prompted.

fixSteps.title: Verify
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm app reports successful calibration and restart drone.

whenToCallPro: If calibration fails repeatedly in clean environments, the compass sensor may be damaged and require board-level service.

faq.q: Can I fly with a compass error?
faq.a: Only in ATTI mode without GPS, which is not recommended for beginners.
Extreme cold can temporarily affect calibration; warm the drone before calibrating.

title: IMU calibration error
shortDescription: The inertial measurement unit reports inconsistent gyro/accelerometer data.
fullDescription:
The IMU contains gyroscopes and accelerometers used to stabilize flight. Drift or bias in these sensors triggers an IMU error.

Causes include hard landings, temperature changes, firmware bugs, or firmware updates that require recalibration. The drone may refuse to arm or may fly unstably.

Calibration must be performed on a level, vibration-free surface indoors.

fixSteps.title: Warm up drone
fixSteps.instruction: Power drone indoors for 5 minutes to reach stable temperature.

fixSteps.title: Place on level surface
fixSteps.instruction: Set drone on a perfectly level table with no vibrations.

fixSteps.title: Run IMU calibration
fixSteps.instruction: In app, go to Sensors > IMU Calibration and follow the 6-position prompts.

fixSteps.title: Restart and verify
fixSteps.instruction: Power cycle the drone and confirm error is cleared.

whenToCallPro: If IMU calibration fails repeatedly, the IMU module needs replacement (board-level repair).

faq.q: How often should I calibrate IMU?
faq.a: Only when prompted or after major temperature changes.

title: GPS signal weak
shortDescription: The drone cannot acquire enough satellites for reliable positioning.
fullDescription:
DJI drones require at least 6 satellites for GPS-assisted flight (P-Mode). A weak GPS signal forces ATTI mode without automatic positioning.

Causes include urban canyons, heavy tree cover, indoor flight, or solar activity. The drone will not RTH or hold position reliably.

Wait for satellite lock before takeoff; icon turns from yellow to green.

fixSteps.title: Move to open sky
fixSteps.instruction: Relocate to area with unobstructed sky view.

fixSteps.title: Wait for satellite lock
fixSteps.instruction: Leave drone powered on for 1-3 minutes until 10+ satellites detected.

fixSteps.title: Check for interference
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off mobile hotspots and keep phone away from drone antennas.

whenToCallPro: If GPS never locks in open sky, the antenna or receiver module may be faulty.

title: Gimbal error
shortDescription: The gimbal cannot initialize or is stuck/obstructed.
fullDescription:
The 3-axis gimbal stabilizes the camera. On startup it performs a self-check; any obstruction, unremoved gimbal lock, or damage triggers an error.

Common causes: gimbal clamp still attached, tilted surface at startup, debris in bearings, or damaged ribbon cable. The camera may not respond or will tilt incorrectly.

Most cases are resolved by removing the clamp and restarting on level ground.

fixSteps.title: Remove gimbal clamp
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the protective gimbal guard is removed before powering on.

fixSteps.title: Level surface restart
fixSteps.instruction: Place drone on flat surface and power cycle.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for debris
fixSteps.instruction: Gently blow out any dust; check for hair or grass in gimbal arms.

fixSteps.title: Gimbal calibration
fixSteps.instruction: Run Gimbal Calibration in DJI app if error persists.

whenToCallPro: If gimbal is physically bent or won't calibrate, send to DJI repair to avoid damage.
videoSearchQuery: DJI drone gimbal error fix calibration

faq.q: Can I fly with gimbal error?
faq.a: Yes, but video will be unusable and other errors may follow.

title: Remote controller disconnected
shortDescription: The drone lost communication with the remote controller.
fullDescription:
If signal between drone and RC is lost, the drone initiates Failsafe (hover, land, or RTH depending on settings).

Causes include out-of-range flight, antenna pointing wrong way, dead RC battery, firmware mismatch, or 2.4/5.8 GHz interference.

Reconnection usually occurs automatically when signal is restored; otherwise re-pair using Linking button.

fixSteps.title: Check RC battery
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure RC has charge and is powered on.

fixSteps.title: Align antennas
fixSteps.instruction: Point RC antennas toward drone, not at it.

fixSteps.title: Re-pair RC
fixSteps.instruction: Press linking button on drone and RC simultaneously until paired.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Update both drone and RC firmware to matching versions.

whenToCallPro: If RC fails to link even with fresh firmware, internal radio module may be damaged.

faq.a: Yes if RTH is enabled and home point set.

title: Aircraft disconnected
shortDescription: The RC has lost contact with the drone while it may still be powered.
fullDescription:
Differs from RC disconnect in that the drone specifically stops responding — could be powered off, crashed, or in extreme interference.

If the drone is still flying, it enters Failsafe. If landed or crashed, you'll need to retrieve it. Use Find My Drone in DJI Fly to see last known GPS location.

Always check battery level before flight and keep within signal range.

fixSteps.title: Check last known location
fixSteps.instruction: Open Find My Drone in DJI Fly to see GPS coordinates.

fixSteps.title: Wait for reconnect
fixSteps.instruction: If in flight, wait 30 seconds as drone may auto-RTH.

fixSteps.title: Locate and retrieve
fixSteps.instruction: Walk to last known location; beeps help find in grass.

fixSteps.title: Re-pair after recovery
fixSteps.instruction: Link drone and RC once both are powered.

whenToCallPro: If drone is physically damaged from crash, professional inspection is advised.

title: Low battery RTH activated
shortDescription: The drone is automatically returning home due to low battery.
fullDescription:
When battery drops to the calculated minimum needed to reach home, the drone initiates RTH automatically. You have 10 seconds to cancel but cancellation does not restore battery and will force landing.

RTH flies at a preset altitude directly to home point. Obstacle avoidance may be active depending on model.

If battery gets critically low mid-return, drone will land immediately wherever it is.

fixSteps.title: Do not cancel RTH
fixSteps.instruction: Let drone return unless you can land safely nearby quickly.

fixSteps.title: Monitor descent
fixSteps.instruction: Watch map and telemetry until drone lands.

fixSteps.title: Replace battery
fixSteps.instruction: Swap to charged battery for next flight.

fixSteps.title: Check battery health
fixSteps.instruction: In app review battery cycles; replace if swelling or >200 cycles and fast drain.

whenToCallPro: Not applicable — this is normal behavior, not a fault.

faq.q: Can I cancel low battery RTH?
faq.a: Yes briefly, but critical landing will still occur.
Fly in no wind, warm temps, and keep weight low.

title: Motor error
shortDescription: One of the brushless motors is not spinning correctly or is obstructed.
fullDescription:
DJI ESCs monitor each motor. If current draw is too high or rotation too slow, a motor error is raised and the motor stops for safety.

Causes include tangled grass/hair, damaged bearings, broken propeller stuck, water damage, or burnt ESC.

Inspect motor before restart — forcing spin can damage ESC.

fixSteps.title: Inspect motor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove propeller and spin motor by hand — it should turn freely and silently.

fixSteps.title: Clean debris
fixSteps.instruction: Use compressed air and tweezers to remove grass/hair from motor bell.

fixSteps.title: Lubricate if gritty
fixSteps.instruction: Apply tiny drop of sewing machine oil to bearings (not recommended by DJI but works).

fixSteps.title: Professional replacement
fixSteps.instruction: If motor is burnt or bearings destroyed, replace motor assembly.

whenToCallPro: ESC replacement requires board-level soldering and recalibration; send to DJI.

faq.q: Can I fly with 1 motor warning?
faq.a: No — quadcopter cannot fly with a bad motor.

title: Propeller error
shortDescription: A propeller is loose, damaged, or incorrectly installed.
fullDescription:
The drone detects abnormal vibration or uneven thrust indicating a propeller problem.

Propellers must be correctly matched to their position (CW/CCW) and fully seated. Damaged or chipped propellers cause vibration that the drone flags.

Always inspect propellers before flight; they are cheap and critical.

fixSteps.title: Inspect all propellers
fixSteps.instruction: Check each blade for chips, cracks, or warp.

fixSteps.title: Replace damaged props
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in new DJI propellers matched by color/marking.

fixSteps.title: Tighten quick-release
fixSteps.instruction: Press and twist to lock until clicks.

fixSteps.title: Hover test
fixSteps.instruction: Short hover and listen for smooth tone.

faq.a: Every 200 flights or at any visible damage.
Not recommended — may cause errors and flyaways.

title: ESC error
shortDescription: Electronic speed controller reporting fault or overtemperature.
fullDescription:
ESCs convert flight controller signals into motor phases. A fault here can be due to overheating, short circuit, FET failure, or firmware corruption.

Signs include one motor behaving erratically, power cutouts mid-flight, or refusal to arm. ESC sits on main board in most DJI models.

Repair requires board-level work; send to DJI service.

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Let drone cool 15 minutes if overheated.

fixSteps.title: Reflash firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Use DJI Assistant 2 to reinstall firmware.

fixSteps.title: Professional repair
fixSteps.instruction: Send to DJI if firmware refresh fails.

whenToCallPro: Any persistent ESC error after firmware reflash requires DJI service.

faq.a: On most DJI drones it is integrated into main board.
Yes — can cause flyaway or crash if flown.

title: Memory card error
shortDescription: The microSD card is full, slow, corrupted, or incompatible.
fullDescription:
4K/high bitrate recording requires fast microSD (V30/U3 minimum). Slow or cheap cards cause write errors and dropouts.

Corrupt file systems, unformatted cards, or full cards also trigger errors. Always format in the drone, not PC.

Keep a spare high-quality card with you.

fixSteps.title: Check card speed
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure card is V30 or higher, UHS-I U3 or U3 V30 at minimum.

fixSteps.title: Try different card
fixSteps.instruction: Test with known-good SanDisk Extreme Pro or Samsung PRO.

fixSteps.title: Clean contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Gently clean card and drone slot with soft brush.

whenToCallPro: If no card works, slot may need repair — DJI service.
videoSearchQuery: DJI drone SD card error fix

faq.a: SanDisk Extreme Pro V30 64-256GB is reliable.

title: Firmware update failed
shortDescription: The firmware upgrade process did not complete successfully.
fullDescription:
DJI requires matching firmware on drone, RC, and batteries. Failed updates leave device in inconsistent state, blocking flight.

Causes: low battery during update, connection drop, corrupted download, or app bug.

Repeat update via DJI Fly; if that fails, use DJI Assistant 2 on desktop for recovery.

fixSteps.title: Charge to 50%+
fixSteps.instruction: Charge drone, RC, and battery above 50%.

fixSteps.title: Retry via DJI Fly
fixSteps.instruction: Restart phone/RC and retry update from Aircraft Status page.

fixSteps.title: Use DJI Assistant 2
fixSteps.instruction: Connect drone to PC, launch DJI Assistant 2, select firmware version and update.

fixSteps.title: Update all batteries
fixSteps.instruction: Insert each battery in turn and update firmware via app.

whenToCallPro: If drone is bricked after failed update, DJI can recover via service.

title: No video feed
shortDescription: The live video from drone to RC/phone is not displaying.
fullDescription:
Video link uses OcuSync/O3/O4 to transmit HD feed to RC. A black screen may be due to cable issues, interference, or software bugs.

Check phone cable first — many cases resolved by unplugging and replugging. Clear DJI Fly cache if app bug suspected.

Frozen feed during flight should prompt immediate return.

fixSteps.title: Check cable
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and firmly reconnect phone USB cable to RC.

fixSteps.title: Try different phone/cable
fixSteps.instruction: Eliminate hardware issue with spare cable or device.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware and app
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure DJI Fly and drone firmware are latest.

whenToCallPro: Persistent issue with all cables and phones indicates RC antenna or circuit fault.

title: Home point not recorded
shortDescription: The drone has not registered a valid home point.
fullDescription:
Home point is set automatically when GPS is strong (10+ satellites). Without it, RTH cannot function and the drone may refuse takeoff.

You can manually set home point to RC location in app once GPS is available.

Always verify home point before launching.

fixSteps.title: Wait for satellites
fixSteps.instruction: Keep drone stationary until 10+ satellites are shown.

fixSteps.title: Set home manually
fixSteps.instruction: In Safety settings, tap Home Point and select Aircraft or RC position.

fixSteps.title: Verify on map
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm H icon appears on map at correct location.

faq.a: Default is takeoff location; can be set to RC manually.

title: Obstacle sensor error
shortDescription: The vision/obstacle sensing system has failed its self-check.
fullDescription:
Modern DJI drones use stereo cameras for obstacle avoidance (APAS). Dirty lenses, misaligned sensors, or hardware faults trigger this error.

Avoidance may be disabled but flight is usually allowed. Clean sensors and recalibrate via DJI Assistant 2.

Never ignore persistent errors — crash risk increases.

fixSteps.title: Clean lenses
fixSteps.instruction: Use microfiber cloth on all forward/back/down/side sensor lenses.

fixSteps.title: Remove obstructions
fixSteps.instruction: Check for stickers, case parts, or dried water spots.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate in DJI Assistant 2
fixSteps.instruction: Connect to PC and run Vision Sensors Calibration.

fixSteps.title: Professional service
fixSteps.instruction: Send to DJI if calibration fails.

whenToCallPro: Hardware sensor replacement requires DJI service.
